correctness.rationale: Self-adjoint conjugate-linear A is represented by complex symmetric M, Takagi-unitarily congruent to diag(s_i). For normalized frame pair with <x,y>=t=|q| under first-variable-linear convention, the complex symmetric rank-two matrix K=(xy^T+yx^T)/2 equals ((1+t)/2)uu^T-((1-t)/2)vv^T for orthonormal complex u=(x+y)/sqrt(2(1+t)),v=(x-y)/sqrt(2(1-t)) (limit t=1 separately), so K has singular values (1+t)/2,(1-t)/2. Von Neumann trace majorization bounds |tr(MK)| by the proposed affine combination of s1,s2. Witness x=alpha e1+i beta e2,y=alpha e1-i beta e2, alpha²=(1+t)/2, beta²=(1-t)/2 attains equality. For any q, an isotropic x for the complex quadratic form x^T M x exists; since n>=3 take a unit z orthogonal to both x and Ax, giving a valid y with zero numerical value. The constrained two-frame manifold is connected and compact, and simultaneous rotation yields full circular symmetry, so all moduli from zero to maximal are attained: a closed disk. Independently checked 105 top-two equality cases, 2,625 randomized admissible upper-bound frames and spectral extraction. Finite numeric checks corroborate the all-dimensional matrix argument.
residual_risks: n>=3 is essential for zero-attainment argument; no extension to all nonsymmetric matrices or dim2 annulus is implied.

value.rationale: The constrained q-numerical disk is a natural operator-theoretic invariant. An exact affine spectral response identifies precisely which singular values survive q-variation and provides a complete reconstruction/invisibility theorem for self-adjoint antilinear operators, beyond the known qualitative disk geometry.
residual_risks: It is a subclass calculation; standard matrix trace inequality is an input, and the disk shape is already known.

final_claim: For every finite-dimensional symmetric-coefficient antilinear operator A on complex dimension at least three, the constrained q-numerical range is a centered disk with radius ((1+|q|)s1+(1-|q|)s2)/2, detecting exactly the top two Takagi singular values.
limitations: Complex dimension n>=3, self-adjoint antilinear matrices only.
Other singular values are invisible; no nonlinear/nonnormal full q-range formula.
